Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Hi Priya / Tom — thanks again for the deep-dive today. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed on so we have a shared reference. Please shout if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Intermittent 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during peak trading windows (you reported 95p up to ~800ms for single-turn generation at ~512 tokens).
- Throughput scaling: bursts of traffic up to ~200 QPS with sustained windows at ~50–80 QPS; current infra can't autoscale fast enough.
- Cost sensitivity: need to keep inference unit economics predictable while meeting latency SLOs.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and encryption at rest are hard requirements for production.

Goals we aligned on:
- SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency <= 200ms for single-turn 512-token workloads (with a tiered fallback for >512).
- Throughput: handle bursts to 200 QPS with graceful degradation and <1% error rate.
- Availability: >=99.9% regional SLA for the inference path.
- Security: KMS-managed keys, VPC peering or Private deployment option for later stages.

Model & workload specifics:
- Primary model: Llama-3 family preference (13B) — you'd like a quantized 4-bit profile for cost; fallback to higher-precision instance for evaluation workloads.
- Typical prompt length: 200–700 tokens; avg output ~120 tokens.
- Multi-turn chat: want KV caching to avoid re-generation overhead between turns.
- Determinism not required; small quality delta acceptable if latency/cost improves.

Suggested deployment topology (initial proposal):
- Redwood Dedicated in us-west1 for primary serving (predictable capacity), with autoscaling pools sized for baseline + burst reserve.
- Prefix/KV caching layer to reduce per-token compute on repeated session activity.
- Multi-region failover to us-east1 for DR; cross-region replication of model artifacts, but inference pinned to single region during normal ops.
- Network: VPC peering + allowlisted IPs for callbacks; TLS mutual auth for any private endpoints.
- Security: KMS for keys, SOC 2 evidence handoff next step (we can provide our SOC 2 packs).

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
- Priya/Tom: share network diagram and firewall rules (you mentioned an internal diagram) — ETA: EOD Thurs (attached if available).
- Aditya: propose an initial test plan + sample payloads for benchmarking.
- Marissa: schedule 30–45m follow-up to review test results and map procurement path (I’ll send invites).
- Agreement: confirm NDA/SOW path if we need to exchange sensitive artifacts.

Attachments: I referenced an initial test plan (we’ll produce) and would appreciate your network diagram.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Priya — received the network diagram. A few technical clarifications and a proposed test plan so we can move quickly:

Clarifications:
- If you can share 1) a representative sample request/response payload and 2) QPS profile (per-hour distribution) that will help us tune batching and cold-start behavior.
- Do you expect most requests to be single-turn or multi-turn? You said both — please estimate percent traffic for each.
- Any hard constraints on outbound IP ranges or need for mTLS to your internal telemetry?

Proposed initial test plan (we’ll produce a short PDF — attaching a draft):
1) Baseline smoke run (single-node): 50 concurrent clients, 20 QPS sustained for 10m, record p50/p95/p99 and memory/GPU utilization.
2) Burst test: ramp to 200 QPS over 60s, hold 3m, observe autoscale behavior and queueing latency.
3) Multi-turn KV cache scenario: 1k sessions, avg 3 turns, validate KV cache hit rate and effective token reduction.
4) Quantization runs: evaluate 4-bit vs fp16 for quality vs latency tradeoffs on your 512-token samples.

Deliverables & owners:
- Redwood (Aditya): runbook for the test, sample k6 scripts, initial benchmark results, recommended kernel/quantization profile.
- Acme (Priya/Tom): sample payloads, QPS profile, allowlist for test IPs.
- Timeline: aim for a smoke run week of 2026-03-15; full performance window to align to your 3/22 start.
